observation.visible_scene: A slow-motion close-up of a metallic hammer head positioned over a gray gravel surface, surrounded by a dense white dust/powder cloud. Several brown fragments with pale yellow interiors (resembling cracked shell/kernel pieces) are suspended in mid-air to the right of the hammer. The scene is already mid-event at t=0: the strike itself is not shown.
visible_changes: The hammer head gradually rises/rebounds upward relative to the ground across the sequence (its lower edge moves from near the dust cloud at t=0 to higher in the frame by t=3.2), revealing more of its neck.
A large brown chunk on the right rotates and translates rightward and upward, leaving the frame around t=0.16–0.18; smaller yellow flecks also drift right and fade.
A curved brown shell-half settles at the center of the ground and remains stationary from about t=0.10 to the end.
The white dust cloud is densest at t=0 and progressively thins, disperses, and settles onto the gravel over the clip.
The background gravel texture and frame edges stay fixed, indicating the apparent motion is object motion, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual moment of impact and the downward stroke of the hammer (occurred before t=0).
Where the flying debris ultimately lands after exiting the frame.
Whether the hammer's upward movement is a free rebound or a deliberate lift by an unseen operator.
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the debris (nut/seed shell vs. other brittle object) cannot be confirmed.
Precise vertical trajectory of the hammer (rebound vs. retraction) is inferred only from its changing height within the static frame.
Some apparent motion of small particles may be dust drift rather than distinct objects.
